title: Tourist Profile Segmentation through Symmetric Asymmetric Multivariate Structures: Integrating Biplot, Co-Inertia Analysis and Neutrosophic Psychology
content: Segmenting tourist profiles is difficult when motivations, values and intentions interact under uncertainty. We propose a multivariate framework that combines Biplot representation with Co-Inertia Analysis (COIA) to identify both the symmetric and the asymmetric structures that link tourists' motivations, values and behavioural intentions, and we apply it to the intention to participate in poverty-reducing tourism. In a sample of 400 tourists, the constructs of the Theory of Planned Behaviour and a value taxonomy (biospheric, altruistic and egoistic) are first validated through confirmatory factor analysis and standard reliability and validity metrics, and then related through regression models that also test moderating effects. Intention to participate in poverty-reducing tourism is positively associated with several predictors, most strongly with biospheric values, a result corroborated by structural equation modelling. The Biplot and COIA representations show that this association is configured by a mix of symmetric and asymmetric relations rather than a single linear pattern. We then read the findings through neutrosophic psychology, which represents the truth, indeterminacy and falsity of each attitude, to model the uncertainty in tourist motivations. The framework offers a finer-grained basis for tourism segmentation and for decision-making under uncertainty.
